explain.title: Cell wall
explain.body: The cells of bacteria, fungi, plants and some protists (algae) have a rigid non-living wall around cell membrane. It is called cell wall. It provides shape, strength, protection and support to the inner living matter (protoplasm) of the cell. Plant walls have a middle lamella, primary wall and secondary wall. Plasmodesmata are channels that allow molecule exchange between adjacent cells.

explain.title: Cell membrane
explain.body: All cells have a thin and elastic cell membrane around the cytoplasm. It is selectively-permeable. It allows very few molecules to pass through it while blocks many other molecules. Its fluid-mosaic model has a fluid-like lipid bilayer with proteins submerged in it; lipids and proteins can move laterally.

explain.title: Cytoplasm and nucleus
explain.body: It is the jelly-like substance that fills the inside of a cell. Cytoplasm provides a medium for organelles to move and function and is a site for metabolic reactions. The nucleus is the cell’s control center; its DNA contains genes that control cell activities and transmit characteristics.

explain.title: Cell structures that make and move materials
explain.body: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis. Rough ER has ribosomes and functions in protein synthesis; smooth ER lacks ribosomes and is involved in lipid metabolism, transport and detoxification. The Golgi apparatus modifies proteins and packs them into vesicles.

explain.title: Energy, storage and movement
explain.body: Mitochondria produce ATP during aerobic respiration. Chloroplasts capture light energy and use it to prepare glucose. Vacuoles store fluid and other materials; the large central vacuole in mature plant cells helps keep them turgid. Cilia and flagella function in movement.

mistakes: Do not say that the cell wall is living; the textbook describes it as rigid and non-living.

Do not say that nucleoli control the cell: ribosomes are assembled there, while the nucleus directs cellular activities.
Do not confuse rough ER with smooth ER: rough ER has ribosomes; smooth ER lacks them.
Do not confuse mitochondrial cristae with chloroplast grana or thylakoids.

explain.title: Specialization makes cells suited to their jobs

explain.title: Plant cells have specialized roles
explain.body: Mesophyll cells contain many chloroplasts and are specialized for photosynthesis. Root hair cells increase surface area for absorbing water and minerals. Guard cells regulate the opening and closing of leaf stomata.

explain.title: Animal cells have specialized structures and functions
explain.body: Muscle cells contract; neurons transmit nerve impulses; red blood cells carry oxygen; and liver cells perform functions including detoxification, storage, and production of blood-clotting proteins.

explain.body: Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration and release energy. Cristae increase the inner surface area for respiration. Lysosomes use digestive enzymes to break down waste. The cytoskeleton helps maintain cell shape.

explain.title: Plant-cell features
explain.body: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall and usually a large central vacuole; many also have chloroplasts for photosynthesis. Water entering by osmosis causes the cell contents to press against the wall, creating turgor pressure.

explain.title: Specialization in multicellular organisms
explain.body: Different cells are adapted for different jobs. Mesophyll cells make glucose by photosynthesis, nerve cells send signals, and other specialized cells contribute to division of labour in the organism.

mistakes: Do not confuse the nucleolus, which assembles ribosome components, with chromatin, which contains DNA and proteins.
Do not say that ribosomes make lipids: ribosomes make proteins, while smooth ER is associated with lipid synthesis.
Do not confuse rough ER with smooth ER: rough ER has ribosomes; smooth ER does not.
When describing a plant cell wall, name cellulose; fungal walls contain chitin and bacterial walls contain peptidoglycan.
For a comparison, do not list features without saying which cell type has each feature.
When explaining turgor pressure, include water entering by osmosis and the cell wall resisting the pressure.

notes.title: 3.1 Cell
notes.answer: The cell is the basic unit of life.
notes.explanation: Living things are made of cells. Cells carry out the functions needed for life. Most cells are too small to see without a microscope, although a few are large enough to see with the naked eye.
notes.simple: Cells are tiny building blocks that make up living things and do the work needed to keep them alive.
examples: The ostrich egg cell is large enough to be seen with the naked eye.
A cell is like a city: different structures do different jobs, while the nucleus directs the cell's activities.
steps: Remember that the cell is the basic unit of life.
Explain that living organisms are made of cells.
Add that cells carry out the functions necessary for life.
notes.checkQuestion: What is the basic unit of life?
notes.checkAnswer: Cells are the building blocks of living organisms and carry out the functions needed for life.

notes.title: Cell structures and their functions
notes.answer: Cell structures have different features and functions. For example, the cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell, while the nucleus directs cellular activities.
notes.explanation: A cell has structures that each perform particular jobs. Some provide support or control what enters and leaves; others store materials, make proteins, or help the cell move. Knowing each structure’s location and function helps you explain how a cell works.
notes.simple: Think of a cell as a tiny working unit. Its parts have different jobs, like protecting it, controlling it, or moving materials.
examples: The cell wall gives plant cells strength and support.
The nucleus contains DNA and directs cell activities.
steps: Identify the cell structure named in the question.
Recall its key feature or location.
State its function clearly, using the textbook’s terms.
notes.checkQuestion: What are the channels in plant cell walls that allow molecules to pass between adjacent cells called?
notes.checkAnswer: Plasmodesmata are channels in cell walls that allow molecules to pass between adjacent cells.

notes.title: Structural advantages of plant and animal cells
notes.explanation: Plant and animal cells have structures suited to their jobs. Plant cell walls support and protect cells, chloroplasts make food, and large vacuoles help keep cells firm. Animal cells have structures such as centrioles and lysosomes, and their lack of a rigid cell wall lets them change shape.
notes.simple: Cell structures are parts with particular jobs. Plant cells have structures that help them stay supported and make food. Animal cells have structures that help with cell division, cleanup, and movement.
examples: A plant cell wall supports and protects the cell.
A sperm cell uses its flagellum to move toward the egg.
steps: Identify the structure named in the question.
State its job using the textbook's wording.
Link that job to the advantage it gives the cell.
notes.checkQuestion: Which plant cell structure provides turgor pressure that helps maintain cell shape?
notes.checkAnswer: The large central vacuole stores water, nutrients, and waste products. It provides turgor pressure that maintains cell shape.

notes.title: Cell Specialization
notes.answer: A red blood cell carries oxygen from the lungs to the body's tissues.
notes.explanation: In multicellular organisms, different cells have different structures and jobs. Specialization helps each cell do its job well, and division of labour lets cells and cell parts work together.
notes.simple: Cells are like a team: each kind has a shape and parts suited to a particular job.
examples: Mesophyll cells absorb light for photosynthesis.
Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to the body's tissues.
steps: Cells formed by cell division are initially similar.
They undergo specialization or differentiation and develop special sizes, structures, and metabolic features.
Their features suit particular jobs, such as photosynthesis, movement, or carrying oxygen.
Different cell types work together in a multicellular organism.
notes.checkQuestion: What is one job of a red blood cell?
notes.checkAnswer: Mesophyll cells contain many chloroplasts for photosynthesis; their shape and arrangement help absorb light.

notes.title: Stem cells
notes.answer: Stem cells are undifferentiated or unspecialized cells that can differentiate into specific cells.
notes.explanation: Stem cells are unspecialized cells. They can make new cells that differentiate into particular specialized cell types. Some stem cells remain in the body and help maintain or repair tissues.
notes.simple: A stem cell is a cell that has not yet become a particular kind of cell. It can develop into specific cell types.
examples: Skin stem cells help in wound healing.
Bone marrow stem cells differentiate to make different types of blood cells and immune cells.
steps: Identify a stem cell as an unspecialized or undifferentiated cell.
State that it can differentiate into specific cells.
notes.checkQuestion: How would you define a stem cell?
notes.checkAnswer: Stem cells are undifferentiated or unspecialized cells that can differentiate into specific cells.

notes.title: Cell structures and their functions
notes.answer: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.
notes.explanation: A cell has structures that perform different jobs. The nucleus controls cell activities and contains genetic material. Organelles such as mitochondria, ribosomes, the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus and lysosomes each have special roles. In multicellular organisms, cells can become specialized to perform particular functions.
notes.simple: A cell is like a small team: each part has its own job, and the parts work together.
examples: Mitochondria release energy during cellular respiration.
Mesophyll cells in leaves make glucose by photosynthesis.
steps: Identify the cell structure named in the question.
Recall the main job of that structure.
Connect its job to the needs of the whole cell.
notes.checkQuestion: Which organelle is the site of protein synthesis?
notes.checkAnswer: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.

It forms the roads that transport materials.

options: Cells carry out the functions necessary for life.
Cells are visible to the naked eye in every organism.
Only large organisms are made of cells.

quiz.stem: Which layer holds together the primary walls of adjacent plant cells?
rationales: Correct: the middle lamella holds together the primary walls of adjacent cells.
The primary wall is a cellulose-rich wall layer, but it is not the layer joining adjacent cells.
The secondary wall may be made on the inner side of a primary wall in some plant cells.
The cell membrane surrounds the cytoplasm; it does not hold adjacent primary walls together.

quiz.stem: What is the cell wall of fungi made of?
rationales: Peptidoglycan makes up the cell wall of prokaryotes.
Correct: fungal cell walls are made of chitin.
Cellulose is found in plant cell walls and the cell walls of algae.
Tubulin is a protein that makes up microtubules.

quiz.stem: Which structure forms a double-membrane boundary around the nucleus?
rationales: Nucleoplasm is the jelly-like material inside the nucleus.
The nucleolus is a small body inside the nucleus where ribosomes are assembled.
Correct: the nuclear envelope is the double membrane around the nucleus.
Chromatin is thread-like material made of DNA and proteins inside the nucleus.

quiz.stem: What happens to chromatin when a cell starts dividing?
options: The nucleus moves to the centre
The nuclear envelope becomes the cell wall
rationales: In mature plant cells, a large central vacuole can push the nucleus to the side; this is not what happens to chromatin during cell division.
Correct: chromatin condenses and takes the shape of thick chromosomes.
The nucleolus is where ribosomes are assembled; it does not become a vacuole.
The nuclear envelope does not become the cell wall.

quiz.stem: What is the membrane of a plant vacuole called?
rationales: Correct: the membrane of a plant vacuole is called the tonoplast.
A crista is a fold of the inner membrane of a mitochondrion.
A centriole is an organelle involved in forming spindle fibres and basal bodies.
Cisternae are the flattened sacs that make up the Golgi apparatus.

quiz.stem: Which statement correctly compares cilia and flagella?
options: Long and always present in pairs
rationales: Correct: cilia are short and usually numerous, while flagella are longer and fewer.
Flagella are longer but are usually fewer, not numerous.
Cilia are usually numerous, not few.
Flagella are longer and fewer; they are not always present in pairs.

quiz.stem: What material makes the rigid plant cell wall described in this section?
rationales: Correct: the section states that plant cell walls are made of cellulose.
Incorrect: protein is not named as the material of the plant cell wall in this section.
Incorrect: starch is not named as the material of the plant cell wall in this section.
Incorrect: the section says cellulose, not chitin, makes the plant cell wall.

quiz.stem: What is the main advantage of chloroplasts in plant cells?
rationales: Incorrect: making spindle fibres is the role of centrioles in animal cells.
Incorrect: storing water and nutrients is a role of the large central vacuole.
Correct: chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis, helping plants produce food.
Incorrect: breaking down waste materials is a role of lysosomes.

quiz.stem: How does the large central vacuole help maintain a plant cell's shape?
options: It allows direct communication between cells.
rationales: Incorrect: centrioles make spindle fibres during cell division.
Correct: the large central vacuole provides turgor pressure that maintains cell shape.
Incorrect: plasmodesmata allow direct communication and transport between plant cells.
Incorrect: lysosomes break down waste materials.

quiz.stem: Which plant cell structures allow direct communication and transport of substances between cells?
rationales: Incorrect: centrioles make spindle fibres during cell division.
Correct: plasmodesmata are channels for communication and transport between plant cells.
Incorrect: chloroplasts convert light energy into chemical energy.
Incorrect: flagella are involved in movement, such as the movement of sperm cells.

quiz.stem: What is the advantage of centrioles in animal cells?
options: They ensure accurate distribution of chromosomes during cell division.
They let plant cells produce food.
rationales: Correct: centrioles make spindle fibres, ensuring accurate chromosome distribution during cell division.
Incorrect: turgor pressure is provided by the large central vacuole in plant cells.
Incorrect: lysosomes, rather than centrioles, break down waste materials.
Incorrect: chloroplasts allow plants to produce food through photosynthesis.

quiz.stem: Which animal cell structures contain enzymes that break down waste materials?
rationales: Correct: lysosomes contain enzymes that break down waste materials and contribute to cellular cleanup and recycling.
Incorrect: chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis.
Incorrect: plasmodesmata connect plant cells for communication and transport.
Incorrect: centrioles make spindle fibres for cell division.

quiz.stem: What advantage do animal cells gain from lacking a rigid cell wall?
options: They make chemical energy from light.
rationales: Correct: without a rigid cell wall, animal cells can change shape easily, helping with movements.
Incorrect: converting light energy into chemical energy is the role of chloroplasts.
Incorrect: turgor pressure is provided by the large central vacuole in plant cells.
Incorrect: centrioles make spindle fibres, not the lack of a cell wall.

quiz.stem: Which structure propels a sperm cell toward the egg?
rationales: Correct: the section gives the sperm cell's flagellum as the structure that propels it toward the egg.
Incorrect: the large central vacuole stores materials and provides turgor pressure in plant cells.
Incorrect: plasmodesmata connect plant cells for communication and transport.
Incorrect: a rigid cell wall supports and protects plant cells; it does not propel sperm.

quiz.stem: Which feature helps mesophyll cells perform photosynthesis?
options: To absorb light energy for photosynthesis
To transport water through the stem
To carry oxygen around the body
rationales: Correct: mesophyll cells contain many chloroplasts with chlorophyll to capture light energy.
Incorrect: water transport through a plant is not the stated function of mesophyll cells.
Incorrect: red blood cells, not mesophyll cells, carry oxygen around the body.
Incorrect: mesophyll cells are in leaves and do not protect the heart.

quiz.stem: How do root hair cells help a plant?
options: They increase the root's surface area for absorbing water and minerals.
They carry nerve impulses away from the cell body.
They pump blood through the heart.
rationales: Correct: root hairs increase surface area, helping roots absorb water and minerals from soil.
Incorrect: guard cells regulate the opening and closing of stomata; root hairs do not close them.
Incorrect: axons carry nerve impulses away from a neuron's cell body.
Incorrect: cardiac muscle contractions help pump blood, not root hair cells.

quiz.stem: Which muscle cells are branched, striated, and found in the heart walls?
rationales: Incorrect: skeletal muscle cells are long and striated and are attached to bones.
Correct: cardiac muscle cells are branched and striated and occur in the heart walls.
Incorrect: smooth muscle cells are spindle-shaped and non-striated.
Incorrect: mesophyll cells are green leaf cells specialized for photosynthesis.

quiz.stem: Which part of a neuron carries nerve impulses away from the cell body?
rationales: Incorrect: dendrites receive nerve impulses and transmit them to the cell body.
Correct: axons carry nerve impulses away from the cell body.
Incorrect: root hairs absorb water and minerals from soil.
Incorrect: stomata are openings in leaves regulated by guard cells.

quiz.stem: What is an advantage of the biconcave disk shape of a red blood cell?
options: They provide more surface area to absorb and release oxygen.
They allow the cell to contract.
They increase the cell's ability to transmit nerve impulses.
They form extensions that absorb minerals from soil.
rationales: Correct: the biconcave shape provides more surface area for absorbing and releasing oxygen.
Incorrect: contraction is a specialized function of muscle cells.
Incorrect: neurons transmit nerve impulses; this is not the function of red blood cell shape.
Incorrect: root hair cells form extensions that absorb water and minerals.

quiz.stem: Which is one of the specialized functions of liver cells?
rationales: Correct: liver cells help detoxify toxic substances.
Incorrect: neurons transmit nerve impulses.
Incorrect: mesophyll cells are specialized for photosynthesis.
Incorrect: skeletal muscle contractions move the skeleton.

quiz.stem: What does division of labour within a cell mean?
options: Each organelle carries out a distinct function needed for the cell.
All organelles perform exactly the same task.
Only the nucleus contributes to cell survival.
Organelles work only in multicellular organisms.
rationales: Correct: different organelles carry out distinct functions that contribute to the cell's survival and functioning.
Incorrect: organelles have different functions rather than all doing the same task.
Incorrect: the textbook describes several organelles contributing to cell survival, not only the nucleus.
Incorrect: organelles perform their functions within cells, including cells of single-celled organisms.

quiz.stem: What is the main specialized function of red blood cells?
options: They are specialized to carry oxygen from the lungs to body tissues.
They contract to move food through the alimentary canal.
They make extensions that absorb water from soil.
They receive nerve impulses and send them to the cell body.
rationales: Correct: red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to the body's tissues.
Incorrect: smooth muscle cells in the alimentary canal contract to move food forward.
Incorrect: root hair cells absorb water and minerals from soil.
Incorrect: dendrites receive nerve impulses and transmit them to the cell body.

quiz.stem: Which description best defines a stem cell?
options: A specialized cell that cannot make new cells
An unspecialized cell that can differentiate into specialized cells
A cell found only in the skin
rationales: This is not the section's definition of a stem cell.
This is correct because stem cells are unspecialized and can differentiate into specialized cells.
Stem cells are found in different parts of the body, not only in the skin.
Carrying oxygen is a function of red blood cells, not the definition of a stem cell.

quiz.stem: Which cell is described as the earliest stem cell in development?
rationales: The zygote is identified as the earliest stem cell.
A red blood cell is a specialized cell, not the earliest stem cell.
A nerve cell is a specialized cell that develops from stem-cell lineages.
A muscle cell is a specialized cell that develops from stem-cell lineages.

quiz.stem: What do adult stem cells in the gut and bone marrow regularly do?
options: They produce new tissues for maintenance and repair.
They transport carbon dioxide to the lungs.
They make the primary cell wall.
rationales: This is correct: they regularly divide to produce new tissues for maintenance and repair.
Transporting carbon dioxide is a function of red blood cells.
The section does not describe stem cells as making the primary cell wall.
Photosynthesis is carried out by chloroplasts, not adult stem cells.

quiz.stem: What is one role of stem cells present in the skin?
options: They produce gametes in every tissue.
They carry oxygen from the lungs.
rationales: This is correct: skin stem cells help in wound healing.
The section does not say that skin stem cells produce gametes in every tissue.
Carrying oxygen from the lungs is a function of red blood cells.
The nuclear envelope surrounds the nucleus and is not formed by skin stem cells.

quiz.stem: What can stem cells present in the liver help the liver do?
options: They help the liver repair after damage.
They make the liver carry nerve impulses.
They turn all liver cells into bone cells.
They stop all cell division in the liver.
rationales: This is correct: liver stem cells help the liver repair after damage.
Nerve impulses are transmitted by neurons, not by the liver.
The section does not say that liver stem cells turn liver cells into bone cells.
The text describes repair and cell production, not stopping all cell division.

quiz.stem: What do bone marrow stem cells differentiate to make?
options: Different types of blood cells and immune cells
rationales: This is correct: bone marrow stem cells make different types of blood cells and immune cells.
Bone marrow stem cells do not make only skin cells according to the section.
Bone marrow stem cells do not make only muscle cells according to the section.
Bone marrow stem cells do not make only nerve cells according to the section.

quiz.stem: Which statement about stem cells that remain in the body is correct?
options: They can divide and differentiate into specific cells as the body needs them.
They can only divide before birth.
They can become only one kind of cell throughout the body.
They cannot help repair damaged tissue.
rationales: This is correct: these stem cells can divide and differentiate as the body needs them.
The section says stem cells remain in different body parts throughout life.
The section describes stem cells differentiating into specific cells, including different blood and immune cells.
The section says stem cells can regenerate damaged tissue under the right conditions.

quiz.stem: What may stem cells do under the right conditions?
options: They can help regenerate damaged tissue under the right conditions.
They make every cell in the body divide at the same rate.
They replace the need for specialized cells.
rationales: This is correct: stem cells can regenerate damaged tissue under the right conditions.
The section does not say stem cells control the division rate of every cell.
Stem cells in skin help in wound healing, rather than preventing it.
Stem cells differentiate into specialized cells; they do not replace the need for them.

quiz.stem:
The process of cellular respiration occurs in:
(a) Nucleus (b) Mitochondria (c) Ribosomes (d) Golgi apparatus
rationales: The nucleus contains genetic material and controls cell activities, but is not the main site of cellular respiration.
Mitochondria are the main site of cellular respiration in eukaryotic cells.
Ribosomes make proteins rather than carrying out cellular respiration.
The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages materials rather than carrying out cellular respiration.

quiz.stem:
The smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) is primarily involved in the synthesis of:
(a) Proteins (b) Lipids (c) Carbohydrates (d) Nucleic acids
rationales: Ribosomes, especially those attached to rough ER, make proteins.
The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is primarily involved in lipid synthesis.
Carbohydrates are not the primary product of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
Nucleic acids are not the primary product of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum.

quiz.stem:
Ribosomes are composed of:
(a) RNA and protein (b) DNA and protein (c) Carbohydrates and lipids (d) RNA and carbohydrates
rationales: Ribosomes are composed of ribosomal RNA and proteins.
DNA is not a structural component of ribosomes.
Carbohydrates and lipids do not make up ribosomes.
Ribosomes contain RNA, but carbohydrates are not their other main component.

quiz.stem:
What is the primary function of ribosomes?
(a) Energy production (b) Protein synthesis (c) Lipid synthesis (d) DNA synthesis
rationales: Mitochondria are the main organelles involved in energy release by cellular respiration.
Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.
Lipid synthesis is mainly associated with smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
DNA synthesis is not the primary function of ribosomes.

quiz.stem:
Which cell organelle is involved in packaging and modifying proteins?
(a) Nucleus (b) Mitochondria (c) Golgi apparatus (d) Endoplasmic reticulum
rationales: The nucleus stores genetic material and controls cell activities, rather than packaging proteins.
Mitochondria release energy through cellular respiration.
The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts and packages proteins.
The endoplasmic reticulum helps make and transport materials, but the Golgi apparatus is the main packaging organelle.

quiz.stem:
Which cell organelle is responsible for breaking down waste materials?
(a) Golgi apparatus (b) Nucleus (c) Mitochondria (d) Lysosome
rationales: The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages materials rather than digesting cellular waste.
The nucleus contains genetic material and controls cell activities.
Mitochondria are involved in cellular respiration, not waste digestion.
Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes that break down waste materials.

quiz.stem:
Which of the following cell structures is involved in maintaining cell shape?
(a) Cytoskeleton (b) Centrioles (c) Nucleus (d) Lysosome
rationales: The cytoskeleton supports the cell and helps maintain its shape.
Centrioles are involved in cell division in animal cells.
The nucleus contains genetic material and controls cell activities.
Lysosomes digest waste materials and do not mainly maintain cell shape.

quiz.stem:
Which specialized region of the nucleus is responsible for ribosome assembly?
(a) Nucleoplasm (b) Nucleolus (c) Chromatin (d) Chromatin
rationales: Nucleoplasm is the fluid material inside the nucleus, not the main site of ribosome assembly.
The nucleolus is the region of the nucleus where ribosome components are assembled.
Chromatin consists mainly of DNA and proteins and is not the region responsible for ribosome assembly.
This repeated option names chromatin, which is not the region responsible for ribosome assembly.

quiz.stem:
What is the main function of the nuclear pores?
(a) Regulation of cell division (b) Control of pH of the cell (c) Protein synthesis (d) Control of transport of molecules
options: Control of pH of the cell
rationales: Nuclear pores do not regulate cell division as their main function.
Controlling the cell's pH is not the main function of nuclear pores.
Protein synthesis occurs at ribosomes, not at nuclear pores.
Nuclear pores control the movement of molecules into and out of the nucleus.

quiz.stem:
Which of the following cellular structures is found in animal cells and helps in cell division?
(a) Cell membrane (b) Centriole (c) Plasmodesma (d) Vacuole
rationales: A cell membrane is found in animal cells but does not perform the centriole's role in cell division.
Centrioles are found in animal cells and help in cell division.
Plasmodesmata are channels between plant cells, not animal-cell structures for division.
Vacuoles may occur in animal cells but are not the structure that helps in cell division.

quiz.stem:
Which sub-cellular organelle plays a crucial role in energy production within the cell?
(a) Endoplasmic reticulum (b) Golgi apparatus (c) Mitochondria (d) Lysosomes
rationales: The endoplasmic reticulum makes and transports materials, rather than being the main energy-releasing organelle.
The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages materials.
Mitochondria are the main site of cellular respiration and energy release.
Lysosomes digest waste materials rather than producing energy.

quiz.stem:
In a multicellular plant, which cell type is responsible for the production of glucose?
(a) Xylem (b) Phloem (c) Epidermal (d) Mesophyll
rationales: Xylem transports water and minerals rather than producing glucose.
Phloem transports sugars and other food substances through the plant.
Epidermal cells mainly cover and protect plant surfaces.
Mesophyll cells carry out photosynthesis and produce glucose.

quiz.stem:
Which organelle can double its number by itself?
(a) Ribosomes (b) Lysosomes (c) Mitochondria (d) Golgi apparatus
rationales: Ribosomes make proteins, but are not the organelle identified as able to double its number by itself.
Lysosomes digest materials and do not double their number by themselves as described here.
Mitochondria can replicate and increase their number within a cell.
The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages cell products.

quiz.stem:
Which of these are present on the surface of rough endoplasmic reticulum?
(a) Ribosomes (b) Lysosomes (c) Mitochondria (d) Vacuoles
rationales: Ribosomes are attached to the surface of rough endoplasmic reticulum.
Lysosomes are not the structures that give rough ER its rough appearance.
Mitochondria are separate organelles, not attached to rough ER as its surface structures.
Vacuoles are not the structures present on the surface of rough ER.

written.text: Describe the structure and functions of the cell wall.
modelAnswer: The cell wall is a rigid, non-living layer outside the cell membrane.
Plant cell walls are mainly made of cellulose; fungal walls contain chitin and bacterial walls contain peptidoglycan.
The wall supports and protects the cell and helps maintain its shape.
It resists the pressure caused by water entering the cell and prevents the cell from bursting.
